The '''2024–25 season''' was the 143rd in the history of [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur Football Club]], the club's 47th consecutive season in the top flight of [[English football league system|English football]] and the 33rd consecutive season in the [[Premier League]]. In addition to the [[2024–25 Premier League|domestic league]], the club participated in the [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]] and the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]]. Having finished fifth in the table the previous season, Spurs also qualified for the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]].

On 21 May 2025, Spurs secured a 1–0 victory over fellow Premier League side [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[2025 UEFA Europa League final|UEFA Europa League final]], clinching their first major trophy in 17 years since the [[2008 Football League Cup final|2008 League Cup]]. The decisive goal came in the 42nd minute when [[Brennan Johnson]] redirected a cross from [[Pape Matar Sarr]], with the ball deflecting off United defender [[Luke Shaw]] before entering the net. The goal, officially credited to Johnson, made him the first Welshman to score in a Europa League final since [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]]'s [[Simon Davies (footballer, born 1979)|Simon Davies]] in [[2010 UEFA Europa League final|2010]]. The match, held at [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés Stadium]] in [[Bilbao]], Spain, marked Spurs' first European title in [[1984 UEFA Cup final|41 years]] and secured their qualification for the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/may/21/europa-league-final-tottenham-manchester-united-match-report|title=Tottenham clinch Europa League glory on golden night to floor Manchester United|date=21 May 2025|work=The Guardian|access-date=22 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cz9yney9391t|title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–0 Manchester United|date=21 May 2025|work=BBC Sport|access-date=22 May 2025}}</ref>

The European success came in stark contrast to the club's domestic performance. Spurs finished 17th in the Premier League with just 38 points, their lowest top-flight finish in 48 years since the [[1976–77 Football League First Division|1976–77]] season. They avoided relegation by one place and 13 points, only above [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], all of whom were relegated to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]]. With just 38 points, the club also set a new record low points tally for the Premier League era, eclipsing the previous record low set in the 
[[1997–98 Tottenham Hotspur F. C. season|1997–98]] season.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://sport.optus.com.au/news/premier-league/os91108/tottenham-hotspur-worst-premier-league-season-ange-postecoglou-record| title=What is Tottenham Hotspur's worst ever Premier League season? Ange Postecoglou close to reaching unwanted club record| work=Optus Sport| date=25 May 2025| access-date=27 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2ee3l23ezt|title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–4 Brighton|date=25 May 2025|work=BBC Sport|access-date=25 May 2025}}</ref> The disparity between their Europa League triumph and their struggles in the league drew significant attention, marking the season as both a historic success and a major disappointment.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Anthony Dabbundo |title=Tottenham's Most Glorious, Agonizing Dilemma |url=https://www.theringer.com/2025/05/22/soccer/tottenham-europa-league-final-trophy-ange-postecoglou-future |website=www.theringer.com |access-date=26 May 2025 |language=en |date=22 May 2025}}</ref> [[Ange Postecoglou]] was eventually sacked on 6 June 2025 with a club statement citing the teams' poor overall Premier League performance during the season as one of the key factors behind the decision to make a managerial change.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mokbel |first1=Sami |title=Ange Postecoglou: Tottenham boss leaves 16 days after Europa League triumph |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c391v08kp9ro |website=BBC Sport |access-date=6 June 2025 |date=6 June 2025}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 27 March, Tottenham announced their first pre-season friendly, against six-time European champions [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] as part of the ''"Visit Malta Cup"''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs to face FC Bayern in the Visit Malta Cup |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/march/spurs-to-face-fc-bayern-in-the-visit-malta-cup/ |access-date=27 March 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=27 March 2024}}</ref> A first trip to [[Japan]] for 33 years was later confirmed, with a friendly against [[Vissel Kobe]] as part of the ''[[J.League World Challenge]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Club to visit Japan this summer as part of pre-season tour |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/april/club-to-visit-japan-this-summer-as-part-of-pre-season-tour/ |access-date=25 April 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=25 April 2024}}</ref> In May, ''Spurs'' confirmed they would also travel to South Korea as part of its pre-season tour of Asia, to compete in the ''Coupang Play Series 2024'' against Bayern Munich.<ref>{{cite news |title=Club to visit Korea this summer as part of pre-season tour |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/may/club-to-visit-korea-this-summer-as-part-of-pre-season-tour/ |access-date=20 May 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=20 May 2024}}</ref> Before the forementioned tours, an away fixture against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] was added to the schedule.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs to face QPR in July |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/may/spurs-to-face-qpr-in-july/ |access-date=27 May 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=27 May 2024}}</ref> On 29 May, a fifth pre-season friendly was confirmed, against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs to play Hearts in special 150th anniversary match in Edinburgh in July |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/may/spurs-to-play-hearts-in-special-150th-anniversary-match-in-edinburgh-in-july/ |access-date=29 May 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=29 May 2024}}</ref> All of these friendlies, however, were preceded by a [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] friendly, in which Spurs defeated [[Cambridge United F.C.|Cambridge United]] 7–2, in a game that was played at the team's Hotspur Way training complex.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lucas Bergvall and Archie Gray play in goal-heavy Tottenham behind-closed-doors friendly |url=https://www.football.london/tottenham-hotspur-fc/fixtures-results/lucas-bergvall-archie-gray-play-29535606 |access-date=20 July 2024 |publisher=Football London |date=13 July 2024}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2024–25 FA Cup}}

Tottenham Hotspur joined the FA Cup in the third round, and were drawn away to [[Tamworth F.C.|Tamworth]], the lowest ranked team left in the competition.<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup third round proper draw |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2024/dec/02/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-details-2024-25 |access-date=2 December 2024 |publisher=The Football Association |date=2 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Date and kick-off time confirmed |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/december/tamworth-vs-spurs-fa-cup-date-and-kick-off-time-confirmed/ |access-date=10 December 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=6 December 2024}}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn away again, against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth round proper draw has been confirmed |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2025/jan/12/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-round-proper-draw-20251201 |access-date=17 January 2025 |publisher=The Football Association |date=12 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Date and kick-off time confirmed for FA Cup trip to Villa |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/january/date-and-kick-off-time-confirmed-for-fa-cup-trip-to-aston-villa/ |access-date=17 January 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=17 January 2025}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2024–25 EFL Cup}}

Tottenham entered the EFL Cup in the third round as one of the Premier League teams participating in European competitions, and were drawn away to [[EFL Championship]] side [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Coventry City away in Carabao Cup third round |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/august/coventry-city-away-in-carabao-cup-third-round/ |access-date=29 August 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=28 August 2024}}</ref> In the fourth and fifth round, they were drawn at home to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] respectively.<ref>{{cite news |title=Draw made for Carabao Cup Round Four |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/september/25/draw-made-for-carabao-cup-round-four/ |access-date=26 September 2024 |publisher=English Football League |date=25 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United at home in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/october/manchester-united-at-home-in-the-carabao-cup-quarter-finals/ |access-date=31 October 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=30 October 2024}}</ref> In the semi-finals, a two-legged tie against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] was confirmed, with the first leg at home and second leg away.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup: Semi-Final draw |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2024/december/19/draw-for-carabao-cup-semi-final/ |access-date=20 December 2024 |publisher=English Football League |date=19 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Dates and kick-off times for both Carabao Cup semi-final legs confirmed |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2024/december/dates-and-kick-off-times-for-both-carabao-cup-semi-final-legs-confirmed-spurs-vs-liverpool/ |access-date=24 December 2024 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=23 December 2024}}</ref>
